newsitem.title: USA: Educ Alternatives wins 12 Arizona school charters.
newsitem.headline: Educ Alternatives wins 12 Arizona school charters.

text.p: Education Alternatives Inc said it was awarded 12 public school charters from the State of Arizona.
The company said it expects to serve more than 500 students at each of the Arizona schools with annual per-school revenues exceeding $2 million.
The schools are scheduled to be developed in the next three years and will serve children in grades kindergarten through twelve in the metropolitan Phoenix area, it said.
Education Alternatives said it expects to open three elementary schools in the fall of 1997. The elementary schools will also house preschool operations for two to five year olds, it said.

The schools will be owned and operated by Education Alternatives and staffed with Education Alternatives' employees under a 15-year, state granted charter. Enrollment will consist of families who choose for their children to attend this type of public school, the company said.
"This represents re-entry into managing public schools for our company," said chief executive John Golle.
Since 1988, Education Alternatives has owned and operated The Tesseract School in Paradise Valley, Ariz., which serves approximately 380 students from pre-school through eighth grade.
